First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={2}^{u},\,u=9x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={2}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=9.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={2}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot 9 \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{u} \\  & =9\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{9x}.\end{aligned}
$$
